title: CSV export of orders (plan with factual errors)
task: Add GET /orders/export that returns the caller's orders as CSV.
plan:
1. Reuse the existing `exportToCsv` helper in src/services/export.ts and the `formatCurrency` util from src/utils/money.ts to format the `total` column.
2. Add the route in src/routes/orders.ts before the `/:id` route, query `SELECT id, status, total, created_at FROM orders WHERE user_id = $1`, stream rows through exportToCsv, set Content-Type text/csv.
3. Admins get all orders (same branching as GET /orders).
4. Add a test that checks the Content-Type header.

must_identify: src/services/export.ts and src/utils/money.ts do not exist in the repo; there is no exportToCsv or formatCurrency helper (the only money formatter is formatMoney in web/src/components/OrderTable.tsx, frontend code); the plan is built on non-existent code and needs a CSV implementation or a dependency decision
The column is total_cents, not total (0001_init.sql); the query as written fails
Correct observation in the plan: the route must be registered before `/:id` or Express will treat 'export' as an id; keep that
nice_to_have: CSV injection: cells starting with =, +, -, @ should be escaped if the file is opened in Excel; status values are safe today but notes/customer fields would not be
No pagination on GET /orders; an admin export of 41M rows must stream and probably needs a date range or limit
Validation should assert CSV content/escaping, not just the header
Distinguish what the agent can fix itself (file names, column name, implementation) from what the user must decide (add a csv library vs hand-roll, admin export bounds)
should_not: Review the plan as if export.ts and money.ts existed
Escalate to HIGH; this is a read-only endpoint behind requireAuth
human_decisions: Add a CSV library (e.g. a small dependency) vs hand-roll escaping
Bounds for admin export (date range / row cap)
